items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-08-20
items.q: Well who was with Jack Carey in there? Jack Carey, myself, George Foster, Little Chinese, George Boyd.

ctx.x: That's right, he's on the record with you I think. Yeah, yeah.

I believe. Well who was with Jack Carey in there? Jack Carey, myself, George Foster, Little Chinese, George Boyd. Well I'll tell you about that now. They had a boy, I don't know if he's Kent the Old Man Robichaux or not, but we used to call him Robichaux and he claimed he's a relation to Old Man Robichaux, he played violin at the Larry Theater. He's real light with nice hair. Well he played clarinet with us at the Moes. Played what?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: So, when I got in my band, for some reason I had George Boyd, Aiden Morris, Joe Gable on bass, Walter Preston on guitar, and me on trumpet.

ctx.x: Jack Carey on trombone, I was on trumpet. And they had, first they had a boy on a kind of name Robeshow. He was kind of this old man Robeshow, but he was a young fella. Then after that, George Boyd come in there with him. And I don't know who Jack, I mean Jack had on bass. Oh, yeah, Chester. Chester Zadis. That's who he had on bass violin. So, when I got in my band, for some reason I had George Boyd, Aiden Morris, Joe Gable on bass, Walter Preston on guitar, and me on trumpet.
Who was guitar with Carey? What did you say? With Carey?

items.q: I said like uh, George Boyd and Zeb

ctx.x: I said like uh, George Boyd and Zeb, what's his name, Zeb?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: We're all left together. Walter Prustin, George Boyd, Chester's artist, Lil' Chinese, and myself.

ctx.x: I think that's all. Who was the band? George Boyd. That's kind of one. See, that's how we left Jack. Them black guys pushed me up, you know, to get up our own band. That's how we left Jack. We're all left together. Walter Prustin, George Boyd, Chester's artist, Lil' Chinese, and myself. You see, them times, no saxophone.
